name: Candito 6 Week Strength Program
author: Jonnie Candito (Candito Training HQ)
summary: A six-week upper/lower block for squat, bench and deadlift that moves from higher-rep conditioning and hypertrophy weeks to heavy triples and a final near-max test set. Weights come from your 1RMs, and week 6 is used to deload, re-test or start the next cycle.
evidenceNote: Volume is front-loaded: weeks 1-2 have 3 bench sessions a week with 12 (week 1) or 9 (week 2) required upper-back and shoulder accessory sets each, then weeks 3-5 cut volume sharply as intensity rises to 95-97.5%. That is a classic block-periodised peaking structure. Squat and deadlift get only 1-2 sessions a week and the only required lower-body accessory is a moderate deadlift variation on some days, so leg hypertrophy volume is modest. It suits intermediates who want a short, structured strength peak; max-rep and 1-4 rep test sets run close to failure.

Candito 6 Week Program spreadsheet (author .xlsx, archived from canditotraininghq.com)
Candito Training HQ free programs page (archived; links both files as free downloads)

schedule: Upper/lower split with a varying number of sessions per week: week 1 five sessions (lower, upper, upper, lower, upper), week 2 five (lower, upper, lower, upper, upper), weeks 3 and 4 four (lower, upper, lower, upper), week 5 three (lower, upper, lower). Week 6: skip it and start a new cycle with projected maxes, deload by repeating week 1 without the last upper session, or test 1RMs.

progression.description: All main-lift percentages are of your entered 1RM (the spreadsheet rounds to 2.5 kg or 5 lb, and some sets add or subtract 2.5 kg / 5 lb as noted per exercise). Week focus: 1 muscular conditioning, 2 hypertrophy, 3 linear max overload, 4 heavy-weight acclimation/explosiveness, 5 intense strength (1-4 rep sets at 97.5%), 6 deload or max test. For the next cycle, projected 1RM = week-5 weight x 1.03 for 2 reps, x 1.06 for 3 reps, x 1.09 for 4 reps. Accessories have no percentages and should progress gradually.
progression.deload: Week 6 options: skip it and use projected maxes; deload by repeating week 1 minus the last upper workout; or test 1RMs, then deload or start a new cycle. On a missed required rep the sources disagree: the spreadsheet says reduce that lift's max by 2.5%, while the PDF (11/18/13 update) says drop it by 5%, finish what you can and move on without repeating the workout. Week 2 squat MR10 rules add their own 2.5% cuts.

notes: Percentages, reps, day order and accessory slots come from the author's spreadsheet (archived .xlsx, 2013 version, downloaded and read cell by cell); the method, rest periods, accessory choices, optional-exercise set counts and the failure rule come from the author's PDF. The PDF text says the three required upper accessories are upper back, shoulders and biceps, but the spreadsheet's slots are Upper Back #1 (horizontal pull), Shoulders and Upper Back #2 (vertical pull); this template follows the spreadsheet, and a biceps curl is a reasonable swap for slot 3 if you follow the PDF. Week 5 1-4 rep sets: the reps you get (2, 3 or 4) set the projected max, so take them as far as you can within 4. The spreadsheet's week 1 day 4 formulas reference an empty unit cell, so in kg mode those 70% weights round to 5 kg instead of 2.5 kg; round to 2.5 kg like every other set. Rest periods: 3-8 min on main lifts, 1-2 min on optional exercises, 60 s on week 2 volume/back-off squats. Week 6 has no fixed workouts so it is not listed. sessionMinutes reflects the author's '45 minutes to an hour'.
